```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Pass configuration as a named list in `config`:

```r
rvisPlot(
  type = "bar", plotter = "amCharts", obj = summary_data,
  x = "category", y = "value",
  config = list(
    title = "Quarterly results",
    legend.enabled = TRUE,
    legend.position = "bottom",
    barMode = "stack"
  )
)
```

Configuration is interpreted by the selected wrapper. The same key may be
unsupported or have a different default in another plotter. The table below
lists every property currently recorded in `data/properties.csv`, including
its wrapper, declared type, default, and allowed values. Use only keys listed
for the selected wrapper. The property names are case-sensitive.

```{r config-table, echo=FALSE}
utils::data("properties", package = "rvis")
config_reference <- as.data.frame(properties, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

key_meaning <- function(key) {
  known <- c(
    "title" = "Chart title text.",
    "subtitle" = "Chart subtitle text.",
    "legend.enabled" = "Whether to display the legend.",
    "legend.position" = "Where to place the legend.",
    "barMode" = "Whether bars are grouped, stacked, or shown as proportions, as supported by the wrapper.",
    "stack.enabled" = "Whether compatible series are stacked.",
    "stack" = "Whether compatible series are stacked.",
    "additionalColumns" = "Extra data columns retained for use by the chart.",
    "subchart.enabled" = "Whether to show a secondary overview or range selector.",
    "subchart.height" = "Height of the secondary overview or range selector.",
    "colorize" = "Whether the wrapper assigns colors automatically.",
    "tooltip" = "Tooltip configuration or tooltip field, as supported by the wrapper.",
    "tooltip.enabled" = "Whether to show a tooltip when hovering over the chart.",
    "zoom.enabled" = "Whether to add a zoom slider to the axes.",
    "label.enabled" = "Whether to show data labels on the chart.",
    "theme" = "Name of the chart theme (for apexcharter: light or dark).",
    "pie.donut" = "Whether a pie chart is drawn as a donut (a ring).",
    "graph.layout" = "Layout of the nodes of a graph: force-directed, circular or none (positions given).",
    "line.shape" = "Shape of the lines: smooth, straight or stepline.",
    "color.max" = "Colour of the largest values of a heat map.",
    "node.size" = "Size of the nodes of a graph (pixels), when no size column is given.",
    "node.size.min" = "Size of the smallest nodes of a graph (pixels), when a size column is given.",
    "node.size.max" = "Size of the largest nodes of a graph (pixels), when a size column is given."
  )
  if (key %in% names(known)) return(unname(known[[key]]))
  parts <- strsplit(key, "\\.", fixed = FALSE)[[1]]
  axis_names <- c(xAxis = "horizontal axis", yAxis = "vertical axis")
  node_names <- c(node = "nodes", link = "links")
  subjects <- c(axis_names, node_names, legend = "legend", subchart = "overview panel")
  subject <- if (parts[1] %in% names(subjects)) unname(subjects[[parts[1]]]) else parts[1]
  field <- if (length(parts) > 1) paste(parts[-1], collapse = " ") else "setting"
  field <- gsub("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1 \\2", field)
  field <- tolower(field)
  paste0("Controls the ", subject, " ", field, ".")
}

config_reference$Meaning <- vapply(config_reference$Property, key_meaning, character(1))
config_reference <- config_reference[, c("plotters", "Property", "Meaning", "Class", "Default", "Domain")]
names(config_reference) <- c("Plotter", "Key", "Meaning", "Type", "Default", "Allowed values")
knitr::kable(config_reference, row.names = FALSE, escape = TRUE)
```

## Additional settings read by wrappers

Some wrappers read settings directly from `config` that are not present in the validation metadata table above. This source inventory includes literal `config$name` and `config[["name"]]` accesses. These settings may not be type-checked centrally; consult the named wrapper implementation for its expected values.

## General interpretation

Axis keys control labels, ticks, grid lines, ranges, and scrollbars. Legend
keys control visibility, placement, and appearance. `title` and `subtitle`
set chart headings. Graph wrappers use `node.*` and `link.*` keys for network
elements. Keys such as `additionalColumns` retain extra columns for custom
tooltips or formatting. The exact wrapper behavior is implemented in that
wrapper's manual and source code; values and defaults in the table are the
package's current validation metadata.

When a key is not present in this table, check the wrapper's function
documentation and the `...` arguments it forwards to its underlying plotting
package.
